$comment: Deadwood (tools/content/env/deadwood.mjs). Fallen log: lying along z on the ground, the butt (sawn, with rings) at -z, the broken end at +z. radius: [butt, top end]; bow, sink, lump (unevenness of the cross-section), jag (how ragged the broken end is), stubs (count) with their length and radius. lods: sides round the trunk, segments along it, rings (fractions of the radius on the sawn face), stubs (sides of a branch stub, 0 = none). Collision: one hull along the trunk (bark: heavy wood, as the Kenney log was). See broadleaf.json for the fields.

notes.1: First version (2026-11-11): a fallen trunk the size of the Kenney Log (prop.log), lying along z as it does: low cover. Collision: one hull along the trunk (24 points, bark); the branch stubs do not collide. Not breakable (species have no breakable data; the Kenney log had 60 health).
